decisions.reason: The champagne-gold investigation adds a material treatment while expressly preserving the established architectural quality; it does not change the Hero V geometry or construction rules.

The source confirms the unified letterform result but does not change the E and L construction, proportions, or architectural vocabulary; the material treatment is independently represented by the source Requirement.
Applying a champagne-gold material language to the wordmark does not alter the second V's optical construction method or signature right-arm relationship.
The color and finish investigation does not change the selected kerning, spacing reference, or cadence requirements.
The new material direction leaves the established cap-height and peak hierarchy unchanged.
The champagne-gold finish does not change the requirement that the É accent use the Hero V terminal's exact vector geometry.
The source introduces material exploration without authorizing changes to locked assets or modifying the existing revision-preservation policy.
The champagne-gold treatment does not change the all-caps wordmark selection.
The material treatment does not alter the required shared peak horizon between the fixed Hero V and É accent.
The source does not change the requirement to explain the design focus of each review round.
The champagne-gold finish investigation leaves the shared baseline alignment unchanged.
The source requests interpretation of a material reference but does not revise the earlier comparison-proof format or its composition-review dimensions.
